newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian metals gain on back of world market surge.
newsitem.headline: Indian metals gain on back of world market surge.

text.p: Indian metals on Thursday rose sharply on speculative buying on the back of surging world markets, dealers said.
Physical buying was however ow ahead of Friday's national budget.
Copper rose by 150 rupees to 12,950 rupees per quintal while tin and nickel gained by 200 rupees each per quintal at 34,300 rupees and at 37,600 rupees per quintal, respectively.
Zinc lifted by 50 rupees to 7,350 rupees and lead by 25 rupees to 4,575 rupees per quintal. Aluminium was 75 rupees higher at 7,325 rupees per quintal.

"Earlier in the week market sentiment was subdued on fears that the Indian finance minister may reduce import duty on base metals but today prices bounced back on speculation that the minister may not announce any major changes in import duty on metals," said Sharad Parikh, president of Bombay Metal Exchange.
"Let us wait until the presentation of the union budget scheduled on Friday and the picture will be clear," he added.
